title: SGLang LoRA adapter loader -- T1059 SafeUnpickler denylist bypass unauthenticated RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-15969 (GHSA-2wvm-gjg7-5jfm,
CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL), affecting SGLang, a high-performance LLM/VLM
serving engine.

`/load_lora_adapter_from_tensors` accepts a caller-supplied,
base64-encoded pickle payload representing LoRA adapter tensors. The
endpoint's `SafeUnpickler` is meant to restrict which classes a pickle
stream can reconstruct, but its denylist is incomplete -- a crafted
payload using a class the denylist does not cover reaches arbitrary
code execution during deserialization, with no authentication required
to reach the endpoint at all. This is SGLang's first of several
pickle-deserialization RCEs disclosed the same week (see sibling rules
for `/update_weights_from_disk` and the dumper subsystem), each a
distinct code path sharing the same root cause class: trusting a
denylist-based unpickler instead of avoiding `pickle` for
network-reachable input entirely.

Detection logic flags a request to this endpoint carrying a
base64-encoded body whose decoded content begins with pickle's protocol
opcodes (`\x80\x04` / `\x80\x05` for protocol 4/5, or the ASCII
protocol-0 opcode sequence) -- LoRA adapter tensors submitted through
the intended, safe path do not require raw pickle framing at the HTTP
layer.

Aggregated from 2 independent sources (SGLang's own GHSA advisory + an
independent security researcher's corroborating disclosure write-up,
part of a coordinated multi-CVE SGLang security research series), no
patched version confirmed in the summary available at authoring time --
operators should restrict network reachability to this endpoint until
a fix is confirmed.
